limitations: Future supplier behavior is assumed stable relative to answer-sealed historical observations.
Zero carrier loss observations denote no transport and are excluded from loss estimation.
Initial effective inventory is assumed to equal two weeks of target production.
The one-supplier/one-carrier rule is treated as a soft preference and split counts are reported.
Normalized costs are used because absolute transport and storage tariffs are not supplied.

REQ-OUTPUT-ATTACHMENT-A.claim_text: Supplier-indexed records for the order template.

REQ-OUTPUT-ATTACHMENT-B.claim_text: Supplier-carrier records for the transport template.

REQ-Q1-TOP50.claim_text: Exactly fifty ranked suppliers under the frozen tie rule.

REQ-Q2-MINIMUM-SUPPLIERS.claim_text: Supplier count with exact-MILP or upper-bound status.

REQ-Q4-CAPACITY-INCREASE.claim_text: Modeled weekly capacity and increase from 28200 m3.

REQ-Q4-ORDER-PLAN.claim_text: Order plan associated with modeled maximum capacity.

REQ-Q4-TRANSPORT-PLAN.claim_text: Transport plan associated with modeled maximum capacity.

failure_cases: A structural break in supplier delivery behavior can invalidate historical ratios.
A hard prohibition on supplier splitting is outside the continuous allocation model.
Absolute economic optimality is unidentified without transport and storage tariffs.

uncertainty.carrier_loss: positive historical losses with candidate-specific tail treatment
uncertainty.initial_inventory: assumed equal to two weeks of target production
uncertainty.supplier_delivery: conditional historical fulfillment with candidate-specific tail treatment
